name: Ferrofluid Dermal Infiltration Drone FDID-6 'Ironblush'
description:
The FDID-6 is a close-range, high-precision drone developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC as an evolution of their medical ferrofluid delivery research. It carries a pressurized reservoir of bioactive ferrofluid — a suspension of iron-oxide nanoparticles in a carrier medium engineered for rapid transdermal absorption — and delivers it in a fine aerosolized spray at contact range. Once the ferrofluid has been absorbed through skin, ZHENG-DAO's proprietary external magnetic induction array in the drone's chassis can remotely agitate the nanoparticles, generating localized heat, mechanical disruption at the capillary level, and interference with nearby electronic implants through induced magnetic fields.

The weapon's name comes from the visible effect of deployment — the ferrofluid carrier medium has a faint rust-red tint, and targets who have been dosed show a distinctive reddening of exposed skin that fades over several hours as the carrier medium metabolizes. The nanoparticles themselves remain active in superficial tissue for 72–96 hours, during which time the drone or any compatible ZHENG-DAO induction controller can activate the thermal and mechanical effects remotely from up to 30 meters. This creates a delayed-action profile unique among drone platforms: the FDID-6 can mark a target and disengage, with the actual incapacitation triggered later at the operator's discretion.

Against targets with subdermal electronics — implants, neural interfaces, payment chips — the magnetic induction effect is dramatically amplified, causing device malfunctions ranging from temporary shutdown to permanent damage in high-intensity activation. This anti-augmentation profile has made the FDID-6 particularly controversial in heavily augmented communities.
specifications: dimensions: 19cm x 16cm x 10cm ferrofluid reservoir: 80ml (sufficient for 12–15 target applications) spray range: Contact to 1.5m remote activation range: Up to 30m (compatible ZHENG-DAO induction controller required) nanoparticle active window: 72–96 hours post-application power source: Dual lithium-ceramic cells battery life: 40 minutes flight, unlimited induction activations (controller-dependent) weight: 1.4kg visible marker: Rust-red carrier tint, fades 4–8 hours post-application
tactical_use: Specialist operators use the FDID-6 in two distinct phases: a marking phase, where the drone approaches a target under cover of crowd or confusion and delivers the ferrofluid aerosol, and an activation phase, which may occur hours or days later when the operator has positional and timing advantage. Counter-augmentation teams deploy it specifically against high-value targets with known neural or combat implants, using the magnetic interference to disable defensive systems before a direct engagement. Military units have used it to mark individuals in crowds for later remote incapacitation without requiring the drone to be present during the actual operation.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's augmented communities — particularly the dense implant-user populations of the Zheng-Dao commercial districts — the FDID-6 has achieved a near-mythological status as a weapon of persecution. Stories circulate of people developing unexplained implant failures days after routine crowd exposure, and a minor industry of 'ferrofluid detox' clinics has emerged, most offering useless treatments but some providing genuine nanoparticle chelation therapy. The rust-red blush of recent application has become an object of paranoia — people with naturally ruddy complexions have reported being avoided on public transit.
story_hooks: Three augmented activists have had their implants fail catastrophically within the same week — the only connection is that all three attended the same public demonstration four days earlier.
A ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC research defector is offering the players the chelation formula for active FDID-6 nanoparticles in exchange for extraction — but they've already been marked.
The players are hired to steal an FDID-6 unit, only to discover the target they're stealing it from has already used it on someone in their network, and the 72-hour window is closing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular hoverdrone with a pronounced central pressure chamber. The silhouette reads as predatory but clinical—all sharp edges and purposeful asymmetry. The ferrofluid reservoir forms a visible bulge along the drone's underbelly, giving it a weighted, unbalanced appearance despite stable flight mechanics.
physical_description.dimensions: 19cm length × 16cm width × 10cm height. Spray nozzle extends 2–3cm forward from the chassis nose. Rotor span approximately 24cm when arms fully extended.
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and deliberate in hand—1.4kg feels heavier than its size suggests, due to the pressurized reservoir and dual lithium-ceramic cells. A weapon that demands respect; pilots report it has a 'loaded' feel, even at rest.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer chassis (reinforced carbon-epoxy composite) with embedded magnetic induction coils. Ferrofluid reservoir is borosilicate glass with titanium-alloy feed lines and pressure regulation hardware.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with oxide-resistant clear-coat. The reservoir window is frosted to obscure fluid levels from casual observation, but the rust-red tint of the ferrofluid is visible as a faint amber glow under direct light. Rotor blades are bare anodized aluminum—reflective and minimal.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant gunmetal gray; accents of deep rust-red (ferrofluid visible through reservoir port), black polymer shrouding, and brushed titanium feed hardware. Minimal branding—only functional labels.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for sustained hand-holding. The launch platform incorporates a textured polymer cradle with rubberized contact points. If gripped directly, the chassis presents a knurled titanium handhold near the power cell cluster—cold, industrial, engineered for gloved operation.
distinctive_features: Pressurized ferrofluid reservoir with graduated etching marks along the borosilicate window
Exposed magnetic induction coil array visible as black wire-wrapped rings beneath clear chassis panels
Twin rotor arms with asymmetrical pitch for precision hover and rapid directional changes
Spray nozzle assembly with micro-adjustable targeting cross-hairs integrated into the forward optics pod
Dual lithium-ceramic cell housings with status indicator LEDs (green/amber/red) visible through translucent port
Faint electromagnetic shimmer visible around the induction coil clusters when powered (subtle but unsettling)
Corrosion-resistant feed lines running from reservoir to nozzle in exposed titanium—no concealment of function
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo (stylized double-helix with circuit pattern) stamped in small raised relief on the left rotor arm. Serial plate affixed to the aft chassis: white anodized aluminum with black laser-etched designation (typically FDID-6–[XXXX]). Regulatory prohibition stamps in Chinese, English, and Russian on the battery shroud.
physical_description.condition_typical: Military-issue units appear pristine and meticulously maintained. Field-deployed examples show microscopic rust discoloration around the nozzle from ferrofluid micro-leakage—unavoidable wear that makes active units subtly identifiable. Some operators file or scratch the ZHENG-DAO logo for plausible deniability.
